q: He proposed that acids are any substances that dissociate to produce ____ ($H^+$) when they dissolve in water.
e: He proposed that acids are any substances that dissociate to produce hydrogen ions (H+) when they dissolve in water. Hydrogen ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Strong acids such as hydrochloric acid ____ ionise in water, whereas weak acids such as ethanoic acid only partially ionise.
e: Strong acids such as hydrochloric acid completely ionise in water, whereas weak acids such as ethanoic acid only partially ionise. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: Bases are any substances that dissociate to produce ____ ($OH^-$) when they dissolve in water.
e: Bases are any substances that dissociate to produce hydroxide ions (OH-) when they dissolve in water. Hydroxide ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Arrhenius theory has some weak points, one of which is that its application is limited to ____ solutions.
e: Arrhenius theory has some weak points, one of which is that its application is limited to aqueous solutions. Arrhenius acids give H+ in water and Arrhenius bases give OH- in water.

q: It is unable to account for the acidic properties of $CO_2$, $SO_2$, $SO_3$, etc., which do not have ____, and the basic properties of $CaO$, $MgO$, etc., which do not have hydroxyl groups.
e: It is unable to account for the acidic properties of CO2, SO2, SO3, etc., which do not have hydrogen, and the basic properties of CaO, MgO, etc., which do not have hydroxyl groups. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: The Danish chemist Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted (1879-1947) and the English chemist Thomas Martin Lowry (1874-1936) independently proposed a new theory, called the ____ theory.
e: The Danish chemist Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted (1879-1947) and the English chemist Thomas Martin Lowry (1874-1936) independently proposed a new theory, called the Bronsted-Lowry theory. A Bronsted acid donates a proton and a Bronsted base accepts a proton.

q: Acids are ____ and bases are proton acceptors.
e: Acids are proton donors and bases are proton acceptors. Proton donors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids are proton donors and bases are ____.
e: Acids are proton donors and bases are proton acceptors. Proton acceptors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An extension of the Bronsted-Lowry definition of acids and bases is the concept of the ____, which consists of either an acid and its conjugate base or a base and its conjugate acid.
e: An extension of the Bronsted-Lowry definition of acids and bases is the concept of the conjugate acid-base pair, which consists of either an acid and its conjugate base or a base and its conjugate acid. A Bronsted-Lowry base accepts a proton.

q: The ____ of a Bronsted-Lowry acid is the species that remains when one proton has been removed from the acid.
e: The conjugate base of a Bronsted-Lowry acid is the species that remains when one proton has been removed from the acid. Conjugate base: a Bronsted-Lowry base accepts a proton.

q: Conversely, a conjugate acid results from the ____ of a proton to a Bronsted-Lowry base.
e: Conversely, a conjugate acid results from the addition of a proton to a Bronsted-Lowry base. A Bronsted-Lowry base accepts a proton.

q: A strong acid has a ____ conjugate base and a strong base has a weak conjugate acid, and vice versa.
e: A strong acid has a weak conjugate base and a strong base has a weak conjugate acid, and vice versa. A conjugate base is what is left after an acid gives away a proton.

q: On the other hand, the $H_2O$ molecule accepts that proton forming $H_3O^+$ ion (____ ion).
e: On the other hand, the H2O molecule accepts that proton forming H3O+ ion (hydronium ion). Hydronium is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The Bronsted-Lowry theory fails to explain the reaction between acidic oxides ($CO_2$, $SO_2$, and $SO_3$) and basic oxides ($BaO$, $CaO$, and $Na_2O$) because there is no ____.
e: The Bronsted-Lowry theory fails to explain the reaction between acidic oxides (CO2, SO2, and SO3) and basic oxides (BaO, CaO, and Na2O) because there is no proton transfer. A Bronsted acid donates a proton and a Bronsted base accepts a proton.

q: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can ____, and acids are species that can accept an electron pair.
e: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can donate an electron pair, and acids are species that can accept an electron pair. Donate an electron pair: a Lewis acid accepts an electron pair and a Lewis base donates one.

q: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can donate an electron pair, and acids are species that can ____.
e: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can donate an electron pair, and acids are species that can accept an electron pair. Accept an electron pair: a Lewis acid accepts an electron pair and a Lewis base donates one.

q: The $NH_3$ molecule possesses a ____ of electrons (on the N atom) which is shared by the electron-deficient $BF_3$ molecule (on the B atom).
e: The NH3 molecule possesses a lone pair of electrons (on the N atom) which is shared by the electron-deficient BF3 molecule (on the B atom). An electron-deficient molecule does not have enough valence electrons for an octet on the central atom, like BF3.

q: The $NH_3$ molecule, which donates an electron pair, behaves as a ____.
e: The NH3 molecule, which donates an electron pair, behaves as a Lewis base. A Lewis base donates an electron pair.

q: The $BF_3$ molecule, which accepts an electron pair, behaves as a ____.
e: The BF3 molecule, which accepts an electron pair, behaves as a Lewis acid. A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair.
